title: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India?
description: Who established Mughal rule in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi?
hint: He defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat.
summary: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

title: When was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
description: In which year did Babur defeat Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat?
hint: It was fought in the early 16th century.
summary: The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526.

title: Who was defeated by Babur at Panipat?
description: Whom did Babur defeat in the First Battle of Panipat?
hint: He was the last major Lodi Sultan of Delhi.
summary: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat.

title: Where was Babur born?
description: Babur was born in which Central Asian city?
hint: It was an important city in the Fergana Valley.
summary: Babur was born in Andijan in the Fergana Valley.

title: What was Babur's original name?
description: What was the personal name of the founder of the Mughal Empire?
hint: His name was Zahir-ud-din Muhammad.
summary: Babur's personal name was Zahir-ud-din Muhammad.

title: Which battle did Babur fight against Rana Sanga?
description: Which major battle was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga in 1527?
hint: It was fought near Agra.
summary: Babur fought Rana Sanga at the Battle of Khanwa in 1527.

title: Who was Rana Sanga?
description: Rana Sanga, who fought Babur at Khanwa, was the ruler of which kingdom?
hint: His kingdom was centered in present-day Rajasthan.
summary: Rana Sanga was the powerful ruler of Mewar.

title: Which battle did Babur fight against the Afghans in 1529?
description: Which battle in 1529 strengthened Babur's position in eastern India?
hint: It was fought near the Ganges-Ghaghara region.
summary: Babur fought the Battle of Ghaghra in 1529.

title: Which autobiography was written by Babur?
description: What is the name of Babur's famous autobiography?
hint: It is also known as the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
summary: Baburnama is the autobiography of Babur.

title: In which language did Babur write his memoirs?
description: Babur's memoirs were written in which language?
hint: It was the literary language of the Chagatai Turks.
summary: Babur wrote his memoirs in Chagatai Turkish.

title: Who succeeded Babur?
description: Who became emperor of the Mughal Empire after Babur's death in 1530?
hint: He was Babur's eldest surviving son.
summary: Humayun succeeded Babur in 1530.

title: Who defeated Humayun at the Battle of Chausa?
description: Which Afghan ruler defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539?
hint: He later became known as Sher Shah Suri.
summary: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at the Battle of Chausa in 1539.

title: When was Humayun defeated at Kannauj?
description: In which year did Sher Shah defeat Humayun at the Battle of Kannauj?
hint: It occurred one year after the Battle of Chausa.
summary: Humayun was defeated at Kannauj in 1540.

title: Where was Akbar born?
description: Akbar was born at which place in 1542?
hint: He was born while Humayun was in exile.
summary: Akbar was born at Umarkot in Sindh.

title: Who became Akbar's regent during his early reign?
description: Who served as Akbar's powerful regent during the early years of his reign?
hint: He was a prominent military commander and guardian of the young emperor.
summary: Bairam Khan served as Akbar's regent during the early part of his reign.

title: Which battle restored Mughal control over Delhi and Agra?
description: Which battle in 1556 was fought between Akbar's forces and Hemu?
hint: It was the second major battle fought at the same place as Babur's famous victory.
summary: The Second Battle of Panipat in 1556 restored Mughal control under Akbar.

title: Who was Hemu?
description: Who was the ruler defeated by Akbar's forces at the Second Battle of Panipat?
hint: He had adopted the title Vikramaditya.
summary: Hemu, also known as Hemu Vikramaditya, was defeated at the Second Battle of Panipat.

options.title: A ruler who claimed the title Vikramaditya

title: Who introduced the policy of Sulh-i-Kul?
description: Which Mughal emperor is associated with the policy of universal peace known as Sulh-i-Kul?
hint: It emphasized tolerance toward different religious communities.
summary: Akbar promoted the policy of Sulh-i-Kul, or universal peace.

title: What was the Ibadat Khana?
description: What was the Ibadat Khana established by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri?
hint: Akbar used it for religious discussions.
summary: The Ibadat Khana was a place where Akbar held discussions with religious scholars.

title: What was Din-i Ilahi?
description: What was the religious-ethical order associated with Akbar?
hint: It was introduced by Akbar in the late 16th century.
summary: Din-i Ilahi was an eclectic ethical order associated with Akbar.

title: Who was Abul Fazl?
description: Abul Fazl was a prominent scholar and courtier during the reign of which Mughal emperor?
hint: He wrote major works about this emperor's reign.
summary: Abul Fazl was a leading scholar and courtier of Akbar.

title: Who wrote the Akbarnama?
description: Who authored the official chronicle of Akbar's reign known as the Akbarnama?
hint: He was one of Akbar's famous court scholars.
summary: Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama.

title: What is the Ain-i-Akbari?
description: The Ain-i-Akbari forms which part of Abul Fazl's major work?
hint: It contains detailed information about Akbar's administration and empire.
summary: The Ain-i-Akbari is the third volume of the Akbarnama.

title: Who was Raja Todar Mal?
description: Raja Todar Mal was associated with which important aspect of Akbar's administration?
hint: His reforms dealt with land and taxation.
summary: Todar Mal played a major role in developing Akbar's land revenue system.

title: What was the Dahsala system?
description: The Dahsala system introduced under Akbar was related to which area?
hint: It involved assessment of agricultural land revenue.
summary: The Dahsala system was a land revenue assessment system based on average produce and prices over a ten-year period.

title: What was the Mansabdari system?
description: Which administrative system organized Mughal officials according to ranks?
hint: The word comes from the Persian term for rank.
summary: The Mansabdari system organized officials according to assigned ranks under the Mughal administration.

title: What did Zat indicate in the Mansabdari system?
description: In Akbar's Mansabdari system, what did the Zat rank primarily determine?
hint: It represented the personal rank of a mansabdar.
summary: Zat indicated the personal rank and status of a mansabdar.

title: What did Sawar indicate?
description: In the Mughal Mansabdari system, what did the Sawar rank relate to?
hint: It was connected with cavalrymen.
summary: Sawar indicated the number of cavalrymen a mansabdar was expected to maintain.

title: Which city did Akbar establish as his capital after his victory in Gujarat?
description: Which planned city became Akbar's capital for a period after his Gujarat campaign?
hint: It is famous for the Buland Darwaza.
summary: Fatehpur Sikri became Akbar's capital for a period.

title: What is Buland Darwaza?
description: Buland Darwaza is a monumental gateway at which Mughal site?
hint: It was built by Akbar at his planned city.
summary: Buland Darwaza is the monumental gateway at Fatehpur Sikri.

title: Who succeeded Akbar?
description: Who became Mughal emperor after Akbar's death in 1605?
hint: His original name was Prince Salim.
summary: Jahangir succeeded Akbar in 1605.

title: What was Jahangir's original name?
description: What was the birth name of the Mughal emperor Jahangir?
hint: He was the eldest surviving son of Akbar.
summary: Jahangir's original name was Prince Salim.

title: Who was Nur Jahan?
description: Nur Jahan was the influential wife of which Mughal emperor?
hint: She played a major role in imperial politics during his reign.
summary: Nur Jahan was the influential wife of Emperor Jahangir.

title: Which English ambassador visited Jahangir's court?
description: Which English diplomat visited the court of Jahangir during the early 17th century?
hint: He was sent by King James I of England.
summary: Sir Thomas Roe visited Jahangir's court as an English ambassador.

title: Which book contains Jahangir's memoirs?
description: What is the name of Jahangir's autobiographical memoir?
hint: It is also known as Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri.
summary: Jahangirnama contains Jahangir's memoirs.

title: Who succeeded Jahangir?
description: Who became Mughal emperor after Jahangir's death in 1627?
hint: His reign is associated with the height of Mughal architecture.
summary: Shah Jahan succeeded Jahangir.

title: What was Shah Jahan's original name?
description: What was the original name of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan?
hint: He was the son of Jahangir.
summary: Shah Jahan's original name was Prince Khurram.

title: Who commissioned the Taj Mahal?
description: Which Mughal emperor commissioned the Taj Mahal at Agra?
hint: It was built in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.
summary: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal.

title: For whom was the Taj Mahal built?
description: The Taj Mahal was commissioned by Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for whom?
hint: She was Shah Jahan's beloved wife.
summary: The Taj Mahal was built as the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal.

title: Which Mughal emperor built the Red Fort in Delhi?
description: Which Mughal emperor commissioned the Red Fort in Delhi?
hint: He shifted the imperial capital to Shahjahanabad.
summary: Shah Jahan commissioned the Red Fort in Delhi.

title: Which city was known as Shahjahanabad?
description: Which historic city was founded by Shah Jahan as his new imperial capital?
hint: It developed around the Red Fort.
summary: Shahjahanabad was the new imperial city established in Delhi by Shah Jahan.

title: Who built the Jama Masjid in Delhi?
description: Which Mughal emperor commissioned the Jama Masjid of Shahjahanabad?
hint: It was constructed during the same reign as the Red Fort.
summary: Shah Jahan commissioned the Jama Masjid in Delhi.

title: Which Mughal emperor built the Moti Masjid at the Red Fort?
description: Which Mughal emperor commissioned the Moti Masjid within the Red Fort complex?
hint: It was built by the emperor who succeeded Shah Jahan.
summary: Aurangzeb commissioned the Moti Masjid inside the Red Fort.

title: Who succeeded Shah Jahan?
description: Which Mughal emperor came to the throne after the war of succession following Shah Jahan's illness?
hint: He was Shah Jahan's third son.
summary: Aurangzeb succeeded Shah Jahan in 1658 and was formally crowned later.

title: What was Aurangzeb's regnal title?
description: By what regnal name did Prince Muhi-ud-din Muhammad become emperor?
hint: The title means 'ornament of the throne'.
summary: Aurangzeb adopted the regnal title Alamgir.

title: Which tax did Aurangzeb reimpose in 1679?
description: Which tax on non-Muslim subjects was reimposed by Aurangzeb in 1679?
hint: It was a tax historically levied on non-Muslims under some Islamic rulers.
summary: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya in 1679.

title: Which Mughal emperor spent a large part of his later reign in the Deccan?
description: Which Mughal emperor personally led prolonged campaigns in the Deccan during the later part of his reign?
hint: His reign lasted from 1658 to 1707.
summary: Aurangzeb spent much of the later part of his reign campaigning in the Deccan.

title: Which Mughal emperor was known for his interest in painting?
description: Which Mughal emperor's court is especially associated with the development of Mughal miniature painting?
hint: His reign followed Akbar's.
summary: Jahangir was especially known for his patronage and personal interest in painting and naturalistic art.

title: Who translated the Mahabharata into Persian during Akbar's reign?
description: Under Akbar, the Sanskrit Mahabharata was translated into Persian under the title Razmnama. Who among the following was associated with this translation project?
hint: He was one of Akbar's senior nobles and scholars.
summary: Abdul Qadir Badauni was among those involved in translating the Mahabharata into Persian as Razmnama.

title: Which Mughal emperor's reign marked the greatest territorial expansion of the empire?
description: Under which Mughal emperor did the empire reach its greatest territorial extent?
hint: His reign ended in 1707.
summary: The Mughal Empire reached its greatest territorial extent under Aurangzeb.
